title: 1991 British Army Lynx shootdown
summary: Army Air Corps Lynx helicopter ZE380 was attacked by IRA units using Soviet DShK heavy machine guns while descending toward Crossmaglen base on 13 February 1991. The aircraft was struck by multiple rounds of automatic fire causing extensive damage to the airframe, hydraulic systems, and cyclic control. The crew transmitted 'We've been shot - follow us!' and jettisoned the underslung load. Despite severe control difficulties, the crew successfully made an emergency landing in an open field with no crew injuries (p. 4, 74-75).
probable_cause: Shot down by IRA South Armagh Brigade using 12.7mm DShK heavy machine guns and 7.62mm machine guns in coordinated ambush attack (p. 1).

factors.evidence: IRA units fired from multiple positions with Soviet 12.7mm DShK heavy machine guns and 7.62mm machine guns in coordinated ambush as aircraft descended to 500-800 feet near Crossmaglen (p. 74-75).

Multiple rounds struck the aircraft causing 'severe cyclic control problems' with 'kicking' and abnormal feedbacks; hydraulic system failure indicated by loss of AFCS and zero transmission oil pressure (p. 4, 74).
Bessbrook Mills heliport was the busiest in Europe with approximately 600 helicopter flights per week, creating routine reliance on low-level operations in hostile airspace (p. 1).
British Army board of inquiry noted that helicopter simulators offered no training in hostile engagement scenarios nor any training in battle damage assessment in flight (p. 1).
Despite extensive damage and control difficulties, crew executed successful emergency landing in open field near Silverbridge with no injuries (p. 74-75).

events.text: Lynx ZE380 tasked with underslung load flight from Bessbrook to Crossmaglen, routed via G30 for mutual support coverage (p. 4).
Aircraft in fast descent through 500-800 feet AGL approximately 8-1000 meters northeast of firing position at 60 knots (p. 74).
Contact ground personnel report automatic fire from east; aircraft crew observes flash in front of cockpit followed by strikes hitting port side behind cockpit (p. 10, 74).

Cabin gunner reports aircraft hit and on fire. AFCS (autopilot flight control system) lost completely; severe cyclic control 'kicking' with strong and weak feedbacks begin; unusual rattling from main rotor gearbox area (p. 74).
During turn, aircraft hit by 2 further bursts of automatic fire. Pilot perceives engagement by 2 weapons: one high-rate 'cracking' noise, second slower 'thumping' noise (p. 74-75).
Pilot transmits 'We've been shot - follow us!' to second Lynx on flight safety net; transmission acknowledged (p. 75).
Co-pilot orders 'Dump it' (jettison load); pilot initially unsure of meaning but realizes instruction is to jettison underslung load. Co-pilot presses cargo release button (p. 75).
Pilot assumes control from co-pilot; begins full instrument check. All systems appear normal except no AFCS lights and transmission oil pressure zero (p. 75).
Co-pilot also reporting cyclic control problems. Pilot states 'OK, that's it - pick a field!' Aircraft now 3-4 km from Crossmaglen (p. 75).
Pilot selects apparent flat long field along line of flight and starts gentle descent with minimum control movements (p. 75).

Just prior to touchdown at 20 knots, co-pilot reports additional cyclic control difficulties. During landing run, cross slope becomes apparent; pilot eases off collective pitch to halt aircraft (p. 75).
Aircraft comes to halt; feels unstable with distinct port lean. Crew completes abbreviated shutdown drills (p. 75).
Second Lynx lands 30 meters away. Pilot confirms no crew injuries to Air Commander and directs immediate Army Rescue Flight callout with strict no-fly order for XMG area (p. 75).
MO informs TO of Lynx 7 down status. Y30B tasked to cordon area. Underslung load reported ditched (p. 10).

cvr.speaker: CAPT
cvr.text: Flash observed in front of cockpit; strikes heard on port side.

cvr.speaker: GUNNER
cvr.text: Aircraft is hit - we're on fire.

cvr.speaker: CAPT
cvr.text: OK, that's it - pick a field!

cvr.speaker: CAPT
cvr.text: No injuries, other than to our pride. Call ARF immediately.

safety_changes: Enhanced pilot training for hostile threat environments
Improved aircraft battle damage assessment procedures
Review of low-level flight operations in high-threat areas

Incident report contains crew statements detailing hostile fire engagement and emergency response
